summary: This script tests whether an embedding model can distinguish between similar and dissimilar text by converting sentences into numerical vectors and measuring how close the vectors are to each other. It sends text to a local Ollama service, converts the resulting embeddings into cosine similarity scores (a measure of how similar two vectors are), and prints out whether related sentences have higher similarity scores than unrelated ones.

explanations.23: json.dumps converts the Python dictionary into a JSON string, then .encode() turns it into bytes so it can be sent over the network.
explanations.24: urllib.request.Request creates an HTTP request object pointed at the Ollama API endpoint, with our payload as data and headers specifying we're sending JSON.
explanations.27: urlopen sends the request and returns a file-like object; the 'with' statement ensures it closes automatically when done, and timeout=300 means we'll wait up to 5 minutes for a response.
explanations.28: response.read() gets the response body as bytes, json.loads parses it into a Python dictionary, and ["embeddings"] extracts just the vectors we need.
explanations.32: zip(a, b) pairs up corresponding elements from vectors a and b; we multiply each pair and sum them up, which is the dot product.
explanations.33: This is the cosine similarity formula: dot product divided by the product of the magnitudes (lengths) of both vectors, giving a score between -1 and 1 where 1 means identical direction.
explanations.36: sys.argv[1:] gets command-line arguments after the script name; 'or ["mxbai-embed-large"]' means if no models are specified, default to this one.
explanations.41: The f-string formats the output with fixed widths and precision: model name left-aligned in 20 chars, dimensions in 5 chars, and similarity scores rounded to 4 decimal places.
